subject.title: [Feature] Configurable connection retry limits and exponential backoff for SSH worker sandbox backend

question: Should initial SSH readiness after `WorkerProvider.provision()` be guaranteed by each provider, or should core bootstrap tolerate a bounded readiness window?
rationale: The current contract returns an SSH endpoint without explicitly defining readiness, while core destroys the lease after its first failed bootstrap command; choosing the retry owner affects plugin responsibilities, startup latency, and paid-resource lifetime.

options.title: Core readiness window
options.body: Core retries classified transient SSH connection failures with fixed capped backoff before applying the existing teardown path.

options.title: Provider-ready contract
options.body: Require providers to return from `provision()` only after sshd is reachable, leaving core bootstrap single-attempt.

options.title: Configurable core retries
options.body: Add cloud-worker profile retry controls after maintainers define defaults, error classification, caps, and provider interaction.

recommendation.title: Core readiness window
recommendation.body: Core retries classified transient SSH connection failures with fixed capped backoff before applying the existing teardown path.
